template.name: mobility_data_publication_prioritization
template.description: Stakeholder interview with a Frankfurt public administration employee working on public transport and traffic data to decide which datasets to publish for citizens, balancing publication/maintenance cost against civic benefit.

sections.label: Citizen Needs and Expected Benefits
sections.description: Capture resident questions and use cases for mobility data, target audiences, desired outcomes/behaviors, and how impact would be measured to justify publication.

sections.label: Current Data Inventory and Access
sections.description: List existing transport/traffic datasets (scope, owner, system), current access methods, refresh cadence, standards/formats, and coverage relevant to publication.

sections.label: Data Quality, Latency, and Coverage
sections.description: Record accuracy, completeness, timeliness, spatial/temporal coverage, and known gaps or caveats that affect suitability for open release.

sections.label: Legal, Privacy, and Licensing
sections.description: Note GDPR/privacy considerations, required anonymization/aggregation, contractual or licensing limits, and approvals that constrain what can be published and how.

sections.label: Publication and Maintenance Costs
sections.description: Estimate one-time and ongoing effort, infrastructure/tooling, staffing, documentation, and process costs to publish and sustain each dataset.

sections.label: Delivery Channels and Formats
sections.description: Decide preferred publication surfaces (open data portal, APIs, dashboards), data standards (e.g., GTFS-RT), documentation, accessibility, and localization requirements.

sections.label: Prioritization Rationale and Shortlist
sections.description: Score candidate datasets on citizen value versus cost/constraints, note dependencies, and produce a ranked shortlist highlighting quick wins and phased releases.

sections.label: Stakeholders and Decision Process
sections.description: Identify decision-makers, data owners, budget/IT contacts, approval gates, and the timeline for authorizing and executing publication steps.

sections.label: Other
sections.description: Anything material that doesn't fit a declared section. Prefer declared sections; use this only when nothing else fits.

phases.label: Rapport and Context Setting
phases.goal: Build rapport, clarify objectives and audiences, and align on what success looks like for citizens and the city.

phases.label: Map Current Data State
phases.goal: Inventory available datasets and understand access methods, data quality, and legal/privacy constraints.

phases.label: Value and Cost Assessment
phases.goal: Estimate citizen benefits and the effort/cost to publish and sustain datasets, considering delivery options and constraints.

phases.label: Prioritization and Trade-offs
phases.goal: Synthesize value, cost, and risk into a ranked publication plan and agree on trade-offs and phasing.

phases.label: Wrap and Next Steps
phases.goal: Confirm decisions, owners, immediate actions, and timelines for approvals and delivery.

issues.description: No explicit place to capture operational/security risks, misuse, reputational or equity risks of open release. Legal/privacy focuses on GDPR/licensing but not broader unintended consequences that materially affect the cost–benefit decision.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a section `risks_and_unintended_consequences` (repeated=true) to record operational/security sensitivities (e.g., infrastructure security, CCTV/ANPR sensitivity), potential misuse/misinterpretation, equity/digital divide concerns, and reputational/political risks. Include this section in phases `value_and_cost_assessment` and `prioritization_and_tradeoffs`.

issues.description: Overlap between `current_data_inventory_and_access` and `delivery_channels_and_formats` around formats/standards could cause mis-bucketing.
issues.suggested_fix: Tighten scopes: keep `current_data_inventory_and_access` to what exists today (dataset list, owners, current access endpoints, refresh cadence). Move standards/format decisions fully into `delivery_channels_and_formats` (future-state choices), and remove format/standard details from the inventory description.

issues.description: Standards example in `delivery_channels_and_formats` is narrow (GTFS-RT) and not regionally aligned, which may bias entries.
issues.suggested_fix: Broaden examples to remain neutral and locally relevant, e.g., "GTFS, GTFS-RT, NeTEx, SIRI" or omit examples to avoid over-steering.

missing_aspects: Operational/security and misuse risks (beyond GDPR) affecting open release decisions
Evidence of demand and feedback signals from citizens (e.g., support requests, portal search logs, past downloads) to substantiate benefits
Coordination/dependencies with regional operators (e.g., RMV/Deutsche Bahn) and inter-agency data ownership boundaries
critique.rationale: Well-structured, with 8 substantive sections and 5 coherent phases whose fractions sum to 1.0. Content is largely on-theme and supports the stated goal of balancing publication cost against civic benefit. However, it lacks an explicit place to capture non-privacy risks that can materially change prioritization, which is a significant coverage gap for public transport/traffic datasets.
critique.next_iteration_focus: Add a dedicated risks_and_unintended_consequences section and wire it into the assessment and prioritization phases.

template.name: mobility_data_publication_prioritization
template.description: Stakeholder interview with a Frankfurt public administration employee working on public transport and traffic data to decide which datasets to publish for citizens, balancing publication/maintenance cost against civic benefit.

sections.label: Citizen Needs and Expected Benefits
sections.description: Capture resident use cases and questions for mobility data, target audiences, evidence of demand (support tickets, portal/search logs, FOI/IFG requests, past downloads, surveys/app feedback), desired behaviors, and measurable impact metrics.

sections.label: Current Data Assets and Readiness
sections.description: List existing transport/traffic datasets with scope, owner/system, current internal/external access endpoints, refresh cadence, timeliness, spatial/temporal coverage, quality signals, and known gaps affecting readiness; avoid future-state design choices.

sections.label: Legal, Privacy, and Licensing
sections.description: Note GDPR/privacy issues, required anonymization/aggregation, contractual or licensing limits, reuse permissions, and approvals that constrain what can be published and how.

sections.label: Delivery Options and Costs
sections.description: Evaluate future-state publication options (open data portal, bulk files, APIs, dashboards), applicable standards/schemas (e.g., GTFS, GTFS-RT, NeTEx, SIRI, DATEX II, OGC APIs), documentation/support, accessibility/localization, and estimate one-time and ongoing infra/process/staff costs per option.

sections.label: Risks and Unintended Consequences
sections.description: Record operational/security sensitivities (e.g., critical infrastructure, CCTV/ANPR), risks of misuse or misinterpretation, equity/digital divide impacts, reputational/political risks, and proposed mitigations (aggregation, delay, rate limits, communications).

sections.label: Inter-agency and Operator Dependencies
sections.description: Identify data ownership boundaries and coordination needs with regional operators/agencies (e.g., RMV, Deutsche Bahn, Hessen Mobil), required MOUs/SLAs/data-sharing terms, upstream/downstream system dependencies, and who must consent to publication.

sections.label: Prioritization Rationale and Shortlist
sections.description: Score candidate datasets on citizen value versus cost, constraints, risks, and dependencies; produce a ranked shortlist highlighting quick wins and phased releases with assumptions noted.

sections.label: Stakeholders and Decision Process
sections.description: Identify decision-makers, data owners, legal/IT/comms contacts, budget holders, required approval gates, and the timeline for authorizing and executing publication steps.

sections.label: Other
sections.description: Anything material that doesn't fit a declared section. Prefer declared sections; use this only when nothing else fits.

phases.label: Rapport and Context Setting
phases.goal: Build rapport, clarify objectives and audiences, and align on what success looks like for citizens and the city.

phases.label: Map Current Data State
phases.goal: Inventory available datasets and understand access/readiness, inter-agency boundaries, and legal/privacy constraints.

phases.label: Value and Cost Assessment
phases.goal: Estimate citizen benefits and the effort/cost to publish and sustain datasets, considering delivery options, legal constraints, and risks.

phases.label: Prioritization and Trade-offs
phases.goal: Synthesize value, cost, risk, and dependencies into a ranked publication plan and agree on trade-offs and phasing.

phases.label: Wrap and Next Steps
phases.goal: Confirm decisions, owners, immediate actions, and timelines for approvals and delivery.

issues.description: Section delivery_options_and_costs estimates costs per delivery option only; it doesn’t explicitly capture incremental per-dataset publish and maintenance effort, which is needed to balance “cost to publish and maintain” against benefit.
issues.suggested_fix: Amend delivery_options_and_costs to: “... and estimate one-time and ongoing infra/process/staff costs per option and incremental per-dataset effort (ETL/pipeline build, QA, documentation, approvals, monitoring).” Also add to current_data_assets_and_readiness: “note estimated effort to make each dataset publish-ready.”

issues.description: Inter-agency examples omit Frankfurt’s municipal operator VGF, which is central for public transport in Frankfurt and could guide stakeholder prompts.
issues.suggested_fix: In interagency_and_operator_dependencies, extend the examples to include “VGF (Verkehrsgesellschaft Frankfurt am Main)” alongside RMV, Deutsche Bahn, Hessen Mobil.

issues.description: prioritization_rationale_and_shortlist is marked repeated=true, but it is a synthesis artifact typically produced once per meeting.
The template doesn’t explicitly plan for instrumentation/usage analytics needed to measure impact post-publication, despite collecting impact metrics.
issues.suggested_fix: In delivery_options_and_costs, add “usage analytics/instrumentation (e.g., portal/API logs, dashboards) and associated costs” to ensure feasibility of tracking impact.

missing_aspects: Incremental per-dataset publication and maintenance effort/costs, not just platform/option-level costs
Explicit inclusion of Frankfurt’s VGF in inter-agency/operator coordination examples
Plan for usage analytics/instrumentation to measure impact post-publication
critique.rationale: Well-structured template with 8 substantive, distinct sections and 5 coherent phases whose fractions sum to 1.0. It squarely targets the brief—balancing citizen value with publication and maintenance costs—covering legal, dependencies, risks, and prioritization. Minor refinements would improve cost granularity (per-dataset), local completeness (VGF), and impact measurement planning.
